questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Great weather, good food, not to far away from home, heard good things about the city from others

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Can recommend going to Rome a lot, I had an amazing time

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I think Luiss was very informative and helpful. They would always answer very quick.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They had a welcome day, where they explained everything we needed to know.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was allright. I had better luck than a lot of the other people. I would recommend to contact some students that are already there early, so if your friend of a friend knows someone that is already on exchange in Rome, maybe there is a way to take over the housing. I found my apartment through airbnb, where we made a contract outside airbnb.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend it. I don't know anyone who lived on campus, so I don't know how that is.  

It is good to find housing near Luiss, because public transport is so bad. I lived in Salario, which was perfect. Also areas like Trieste and Parioli is close.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think its easier to find housing in Rome than in Cph, but still difficult.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Remember to check your KU-mail. They will send all the e-mails about the registration and explain everything.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always write e-mails to get help at their mobility team.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: You have to be ready when the classes are published to register. I didn't get any of the classes I wanted because i logged on 15 minutes after the pblishing time. Luckily more spots were released and I got almost all of my classes. Also you can change classes in the first week at luiss.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register on time, and don't worry - you can always change classes during the first time at Luiss.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was extremely low - can be compared to gymnasium. Some classes were more difficult than others.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot of remembering instead of critical thinking. A lot of presentations in class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Policy Evaluation and Implementation
African Politics
The EU External Action
Population, Environment and Sustainability 
Heritage, Tourism and Sustainable Economic Development

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Heritage, Tourism and Sustainable Economic Development

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You will eat out A LOT, that is were all my money went.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: My gas bill was very expensive. Otherwise it was what I expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't really use any of them.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot, you can find a list.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the welcome week organised by the ESN. That is where you will find all of your new friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go the Lake Albano near Rome or the beach called Anzio. Otherwise travel around Italy - Bologna, Firenze, Napoli - maybe Siciliy or Sardinia

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, though its very different than Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to them in class or sign up for a buddy during the welcome week

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No one in particular.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Espresso, fresh pressed orange juice, pasta, aperol, pizza - so the food :)) and the people are also very sweet.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Dont stress over the academic level, UCPH is much more difficult. 
Join the welcome week to get a lot of friends
Say yes to pretty much everything :)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All of my new friendships <3

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: In may and june it was the heat hahah - 35 degrees everyday is too much. Otherwise just missing friends and family, but time flies.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Good luck!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
